documents.text:
Brookside Training Oval is bright but breezy, with the crosswind carrying the radio booth’s words toward square leg. Tidehaven choose to bat. Noah Vance begins with a ball that leaves Harvey Lane and follows it with one that cuts back. Lane’s stumps open on the second legal delivery. The director stays on the broken wicket for several seconds, so the scorer has a clean first event even though the score strip has not yet loaded.

Rohan Blake sees a different length. He drives through cover for four, then turns two separate balls into singles. A third running picture appears between them, but the camera angle is too tight to show whether it belongs to the live sequence. The commentator calls it as another run while warning that the pictures have been arriving late. Nolan Reed waits padded up as the opening spell continues.

A wide goes past Blake before Miles Sharp is properly settled. Sharp survives two balls, is beaten on another, and is bowled by Vance at 1.1. The run visible between Tidehaven’s first two wickets belongs to the wide. The broadcast then returns to Lane’s dismissal from a stump camera. The two bowled batters are real and separate; the later Lane image is an old angle.

The crowd microphone drops out, and the television feed fills the gap with Blake’s cover drive again. The clip begins after contact and resembles a new boundary if the preceding delivery is missed. The radio caller identifies the same fielder turning at the rope and the same spectator lifting a blue umbrella. Nothing is added to Blake or the team from that insert.

Back live, Blake takes two more singles. A provisional personal card credits six running shots in addition to the boundary because the uncertain picture from earlier and a reverse-angle copy of a later single have both been admitted as live. The broadcast and scorer systems now disagree, and neither version is treated as settled.

At 5.4 Blake edges Vance and Arlo Finch completes the catch. The team board is on eleven when the catch is taken. Nolan has contributed one during the partnership, and an extra is present in that stand, but the booth does not resolve Blake’s personal line. The catch is replayed behind the keeper and from mid-off. Both replays belong to the same dismissal.

The scorer reopens Blake’s early running sequence without announcing a replacement figure. Both disputed running pictures are given separate event identifiers and sent to different camera logs. The provisional personal card remains visible, while the scorer postpones ownership until those distant records can be matched.

Nolan struggles against Vance until 7.3, when the ball seams through and hits the base of off stump. The board has advanced by one since Blake left and now shows twelve with four wickets gone. Caleb Frost comes out to join Owen Marsh. The terminal stump-camera frame is stored under a second clip identifier, a detail that later causes a wicket-accounting problem.

Owen begins the new stand with a square boundary. Much later he collects a single behind point, and another comes from a checked drive into the off side. A running attempt shown between those balls is entered against him by the live operator, although the striker’s-end camera suggests the batters had already returned to their creases when the ball became dead. The scorer marks that entry for review.

Caleb spends most of the passage defending. A pad deflection is initially placed beside his name, and two genuine bat runs are recorded in different overs. One wide also occurs before drinks. The partnership display therefore contains several provisional ownership decisions, while the team progression itself continues without interruption.

When the broadcast first prepares the middle-order wicket graphic, the score attached to Owen’s coming dismissal is twenty-six. The number includes the questioned Owen run and a wide clip that has been ingested twice. The graphic is queued rather than shown as official. No ball number or wicket ordinal is printed on that version.

Arjun Wells beats Owen with a straight ball at 13.2. Owen is bowled, and the new batter walks from the pavilion before the production desk finally airs its queued graphic. The commentary confirms the legal delivery but does not repeat the score displayed on screen. The same sequence later appears beside a technical discussion of Arjun’s wrist position.

Dylan Pierce blocks for seven balls and is then bowled by Arjun on a later delivery. The director places Owen’s dismissal and Dylan’s dismissal side by side. They look similar, yet the incoming batters and over positions differ. That comparison is analysis, not two more wickets. Caleb remains at the other end after Dylan goes.

During the next lull, the scorer resolves Caleb’s pad deflection. It did not touch the bat, so Caleb’s provisional personal contribution falls by one and the run is carried in the stand’s extras. A separate wide remains valid. The partnership now has three extras, though its total and Owen’s residual share are still withheld because the queued dismissal score is under review.

An unrelated delivery check confirms that Owen had also turned a later ball to leg for a genuine single before his dismissal. That live ball carries a different timestamp from the dead-ball running attempt still under review. The scorer files the verified run without restating Owen’s earlier scoring shots.

The automated bowling ticker has also counted Nolan’s stump-camera close-up as if Vance had taken another wicket. A replay technician links the file to the 7.3 delivery and removes the duplicate marker. The correction says nothing about how many legitimate wickets Vance owns; it only rules that the two Nolan clips represent one event. On a separate camera log, Blake’s tight-angle running picture is matched to the delivery already registered as a wide and is removed from his provisional personal account.

Caleb is trapped in front by Arjun at 16.1 after Theo Grant has arrived. The appeal is upheld. The review package repeats the impact frame twice, then the live feed resumes. Soon afterward Theo edges a different bowler, Elias Grant, to Ben Cole. A scrolling ticker temporarily leaves Arjun’s name attached because it has not registered the bowling change.

Arun Cole follows. Arjun returns and bowls him after a short resistance, leaving Tidehaven on thirty-five with nine wickets down. The scorer simultaneously corrects Theo’s earlier line, transferring that catch away from Arjun and to Elias. The change removes a provisional bowling credit without altering the team’s wicket sequence.

The first part of the queued Owen graphic is corrected at the scorer’s desk. The running attempt that had been placed against Owen occurred after the ball was dead, so it is removed from both his account and the team progression captured by that graphic. Its provisional score drops once. The duplicated wide remains unresolved and the corrected card is not yet released.

Away from the wicket graphics, the wide ledger has reached thirteen on the live system. The operator notes that this is still provisional because one entry carries the same delivery tag as an earlier clip. The no-ball and bye columns are not discussed during this check. Play has already moved into the closing overs.

Vikram Holt joins Kian Stone for the last pair. Arjun eventually bowls Vikram on the third legal ball of the twenty-first over. The tenth dismissal ends the innings immediately. A camera action before that ball was only the bowler returning to his mark, so it does not alter the legal-ball count. No final-score graphic is broadcast.

The duplicate tag in the queued Owen card is resolved after the innings has ended. The later wide picture is matched to its earlier occurrence and deleted. The score attached to Owen’s dismissal drops a second time from the original queued version. The same removal updates the ending boundary of the Caleb–Owen stand, but the scorer does not place its starting boundary beside the corrected card.

The card archive preserves all three states for audit: the initial feed containing both disputed additions, the intermediate version after the dead-ball run was removed, and the accepted version after the duplicate delivery tag was resolved. Only the accepted state may feed fall-of-wickets or partnership tables. The earlier cards remain visible to the production team, which is why an old number can reappear without becoming authoritative.

Kian and Vikram’s last partnership contains no batter run. A single wide delivered earlier in their time together is the only addition after Arun’s wicket. The innings had already reached its ninth-wicket state before that extra occurred. The delayed television strip briefly repeats the wide after the stumps are hit, but the scorer links it back to the live delivery.

Another component is resolved from Caleb’s earlier pad deflection. It is retained as exactly one leg-bye in Tidehaven’s innings. The note is entered separately from the wide correction and does not mention the aggregate extras. The team total was never changed by moving that run out of Caleb’s personal column. Much later, Blake’s remaining reverse-angle running clip is linked to one of his genuine live singles and removed as the second duplication in his personal feed.

The innings review confirms that Theo’s dismissal belongs to Elias. It also notes that neither keeper nor fielding error generated a bye anywhere in Tidehaven’s innings. Arjun’s later return is linked to Arun’s bowled dismissal, while the earlier straight ball to Owen and the later ball to Dylan remain distinct archived events.

Only one front-foot infringement produced a no-ball extra in Tidehaven’s innings. It occurred outside the Caleb–Owen stand and was never part of Owen’s questioned running entry. The scorer files this component while the wide ledger is still being reconciled, preventing the categories from being collapsed into one local total.

The wide audit finally removes the repeated delivery tag from the provisional thirteen. The accepted wide count is therefore one lower than that temporary ledger. This decision also explains the second reduction applied to Owen’s queued dismissal graphic. The leg-bye, no-ball and bye decisions were recorded in earlier, separate checks and are not restated.

Before Ridgefield start, the target is described only as one more than Tidehaven’s corrected terminal state. Arlo Finch opens with Ben Cole. Owen Marsh’s first dramatic ball appears to dismiss Finch, caught by Rohan Blake, but the front-foot camera shows a no-ball. Finch stays, the team receives the extra, and Owen receives no wicket from that event.

That cancelled catch is replayed twice during the over. Between those replays Finch drives a live boundary and takes quieter runs. A preliminary partnership tracker credits him with eleven before the first legal wicket, but one of its running clips has the same delivery signature as the no-ball sequence. The tracker remains open.

At 1.5 Owen bowls legally to Ben, who is caught by Blake. This is a separate catch involving a different batter and a valid delivery. The team board reads eighteen for one. The first stand contains one extra, while Ben’s contribution is already fixed at seven. Finch’s share is not settled in this paragraph.

The opening tracker is opened for review during Arun Cole’s over. Its suspected running clip is sent back to the no-ball sequence, but no correction is committed while the chase continues. The first-stand contribution remains provisional on a scorer-only tablet and is not displayed beside Finch’s current live card.

The corrected opening-share note is sent to the scorer’s tablet, while Finch’s current live card continues into the next stand. The interface does not display the two values together. This separation prevents the second-stand replay of his cover drive from being mistaken for another opening contribution, and it means an innings total for Finch must be reconstructed across both partnership windows.

Noah Vance, batting at three, scores on two separate shots after Ben’s dismissal. The shots are several balls apart and together contribute two to the unbroken stand. A boundary replay featuring Finch appears between them, but the unchanged field and the earlier bowler identify it as footage from the opening partnership.

Ridgefield’s chase-wide ledger temporarily reaches eight. One entry has been copied from the opening over’s replay package and is marked uncertain. The two no-balls in the chase are recorded in different overs: the first cancelled Finch’s catch, while the other delays the legal-ball count late in the pursuit.

Before the winning ball, Finch’s second-stand running account shows nine. The scorer then moves one apparent run into the wide column after finding that the ball had passed beyond his reach. Finch’s pre-terminal share falls, the partnership total does not, and the chase-wide ledger remains provisional because its duplicate tag is still unresolved.

At 3.2 Ridgefield have drawn level with Tidehaven’s corrected innings state. Ben remains the only dismissed batter. The next camera action is a replay of Finch’s early cover boundary, and a downstream ticker appends it as live, temporarily moving the displayed chase four runs beyond where the scorer’s book stands.

The replay technician rejects that appended boundary by matching the same crowd movement and bowler. During this pause, the duplicate in the chase-wide ledger is also removed, leaving seven accepted wides across the innings. The two no-balls were logged elsewhere. No bye or leg-bye is added in the chase.

The scoreboard controller waits for the scorer rather than accepting the ticker’s overrun. The controller retains the level state from 3.2, the single completed legal dismissal, and the count of legal balls. Those three channels update independently: removing a replay changes the provisional team display, resolving a wide changes an extras component, and neither operation creates another ball or wicket. Only here does the camera log finally confirm that one apparent Finch single in the opening tracker repeated the no-ball running clip; it is removed, with no replacement inserted into that first stand.

The next legal delivery is the third ball of the fourth over. Finch completes a single and Ridgefield pass the target. That run restores one to his second-stand contribution after the earlier reclassification. No further batter takes guard, and the wicket count remains as it was after Ben’s departure.

The scorer closes only selected ledgers over the radio link. Owen’s legal catch of Ben is retained; the earlier Finch catch remains cancelled and its replays remain historical. The second partnership’s extras can be recovered by separating the opening stand’s lone extra from the accepted chase extras, but the two batter shares are not repeated beside that information.

Much later, the archive operator confirms the corrected Owen dismissal card from Tidehaven’s innings. Owen was the next batter out after the four-wicket state established at 7.3, and no other dismissal occurred between those anchors. The corrected score stays in the revised card produced after both the dead-ball run and duplicated wide were removed, without being paired with the earlier partnership boundary or the delivery evidence.

The broadcast ends on players leaving the field rather than a scorecard. Blake’s personal record requires reconciling live singles and two replay-related mistakes. Owen’s requires separating his genuine scoring shots from the dead-ball entry and checking the revised partnership boundary. The bowling rows depend on distinct dismissed batters and corrected attribution. None of those ledgers is read as a final compact list.

documents.text:
Brookhaven Cricket Oval has a pale late-afternoon sky and a square that still looks slightly tacky. Coral Bay Tides Women have chosen to field. The radio booth can see the venue board, the television strip and the paper ledger below them. The three sources normally agree, though the television operator publishes first and corrects later.

Sienna Park takes the new ball with a slip and a short cover. Elena Cross presses forward while Mira Vale waits deeper in the crease. The first over contains a disputed signal. Television places four runs outside the bat, but the square-leg official is still speaking to the scorer, who circles the entry instead of signing it.

Elena is the busier opener. A boundary comes through cover, several quieter balls follow, and the partnership keeps moving without a clean personal summary. At the end of 3.6, Aila Rowan straightens one through Elena and disturbs the stumps. The completed opening association is recorded as eighteen on the venue ledger.

The stump camera runs twice. First it shows the ball passing Elena's defensive push, then a tighter crop shows the same bails lifting. Tara Quinn is already crossing the rope when the second picture appears. The change of batter fixes both pictures to one event, even though the television wicket symbol flashes again.

While Tara takes guard, a statistician mentions that the innings bye column already contains two. She does not discuss leg-byes or illegal deliveries, and she is referring to the innings-wide category rather than the opening stand. The broadcast moves back to Aila before any aggregate can be formed.

Tara attacks more directly than Mira. Her share of their partnership reaches seven, while Mira contributes two. Two runs in that interval are not charged to either batter. Maris Vale catches Tara from Aila at 5.5, and the live pictures stay with the fielder rather than displaying a bowling analysis.

A replay package returns to Elena's dismissal during the next over. It is introduced as an example of Aila's fuller length, not as current action. Aila is now near fine leg and Nia Brooke is visibly bowling, a field-position clue that prevents the old stump shot from becoming a new delivery.

The commentators use the pause to revisit Mira's first few overs. They identify three runs as her contribution before Elena was dismissed, then switch to her running between the wickets with Tara. The opening-partner share is therefore disclosed well after the stand total and away from the unresolved extras signal.

Rowan Hayes joins Mira. Rowan supplies four in this short association, Mira three, and three sit in extras. At 7.5 Nia hits Mira's pad and wins lbw. The scorer's fall sheet shows thirty-nine for three at that boundary, but the bowler name is temporarily obscured on television by an older Aila caption.

The production strip initially files Mira's lbw under Aila because the replay template was not cleared. The ground desk refuses the attribution. It postpones the correction until the delivery header can be matched with the end from which Nia was operating, leaving the television bowling row provisional for several overs.

Nora Finch arrives after Mira. The new partnership with Rowan begins from the confirmed third-wicket state, though the broadcast does not repeat that score. Rowan settles into rotation and contributes one above sixteen during the association. Nora's component is withheld because a no-ball sequence remains under review.

An illegal-delivery worksheet appears briefly at the scorer's table. Across the innings it currently contains six no-balls. The operator calls that a working count, not a closing count, because one clip may have been ingested twice. The wide column is off screen and no extras total is announced.

Nora's draft partnership contribution is shown as thirty on an internal monitor. It is not read aloud. The scorer places a question mark beside the entry after noticing that one run appears both under the batter and within the no-ball package. Play continues while that allocation remains unsettled.

A partnership assistant has meanwhile written eleven in the extras box for the Rowan-Nora interval. That number is also provisional. It comes from the same no-ball sequence affecting Nora's draft contribution, so the two entries cannot be certified independently. The assistant closes the stand boundary at Rowan's dismissal and waits.

Lena and Nora run hard. Nora contributes six during their time together, Lena four, and four runs belong outside the bat. Emilia Shaw breaks the stumps when Lena turns late for a second. The batting card records a run out, but a fast bowling graphic adds a mark beside Celeste because she delivered earlier in the passage.

The run-out decision remains a genuine team wicket. Only its bowling ownership is disputed. Production asks whether removing Celeste's mark would also restore Lena or reopen the partnership. The scorer says no: the dismissal, fall and partnership end stay; the bowler-credit cell alone must remain blank for that event.

The innings-wide wide count reaches eighteen and the scorer underlines it. The commentary is discussing field placements at the time, so the number is never paired with the other extras classes. A later wide replay is labelled archival and does not alter the underlined category.

Jade Sinclair faces two balls after Lena and does not score. Nora also contributes nothing while Jade is present. Celeste then bowls Jade. A split screen places Rowan's earlier broken stumps beside Jade's new dismissal, similar pictures separated by the run out and by a change of batter.

Pippa Lane follows. Pippa makes six in the partnership, Nora two, and there is one extra before Nia bowls Pippa at 18.5. Nora's personal ledger now spans several partners, but the earlier thirty beside Rowan is still marked provisional and is not carried into a public total.

The leg-bye column is inspected after Pippa leaves. It had been standing at three. The scorer finds the delayed square-leg signal from the opening over, the same unresolved signal that made Elena's first ribbon uncertain, and raises the innings leg-bye class by one. The associated opening-stand extras allocation also rises from four to five.

That restoration changes no team score and no opening partnership total. It moves one run away from Elena's provisional bat entry. Because Mira's opening share was fixed elsewhere and Elena was dismissed at the stand boundary, the remaining batter value is now uniquely constrained without being spoken.

At the production desk, the earlier Mira lbw attribution is finally repaired. The delivery header names Nia, so the provisional mark is removed from Aila's row and retained for Nia. On a separate sheet the fall clerk places Rowan immediately after Mira and identifies Rowan as the fourth dismissal; no delivery marker is repeated there. The editor then shows Tara's catch again, but it is clearly an old angle and carries no new batter entrance.

Ivy Stone joins Nora. Ivy contributes five during their stand; Nora adds four and the interval contains one extra. Bella Marsh catches Nora from Celeste at 19.5. The gallery later reuses Nora's boundary from this partnership, but her dismissal closes the personal ledger before Ivy's final-ball scoring.

The scorer resolves Nora's question-marked Rowan-stand entry. The duplicated no-ball run is taken out of her draft contribution, leaving that component one short of thirty. Nothing is yet said about the partnership's extras box, which is handled by a different assistant.

Ivy and Clara Bell take two from the last ball, one to Ivy and one extra. Meadowridge close on 132 for eight after twenty overs. The close-of-innings screen shows the team total only; it does not display Nora, Elena, partnerships or the extras aggregate.

During the interval, the partnership assistant finishes the separate side of the Rowan-Nora correction. The run removed from Nora belongs in that stand's extras, so the working eleven becomes one larger. Rowan's contribution, Nora's revised share and this corrected interval component remain scattered across three different sheets.

A bowling clerk revisits Lena's run out. Celeste's provisional credit is removed while Lena's dismissal and the corresponding wicket order remain untouched. The clerk has already preserved Celeste's delivered dismissal of Rowan, but does not summarize the bowler's completed analysis.

The no-ball video check also closes. One of the six entries is traced to a replay of a delivery already present in the over log, so that category loses one. The finding is announced without mentioning byes, leg-byes or wides, which had been settled at other moments.

A second scorer verifies that the revised opening leg-bye was the only missing legal signal. The innings categories are now exhaustive and non-overlapping. She checks them against the batter ledger and 132-run total, says the accounts balance, and folds the worksheet before any category sum reaches camera.

One last replay pairs two Celeste celebrations from nonconsecutive passages. Changes of batter, bowler and field between the source clips establish that the first picture is archival. The replay offers no new dismissal and no bowling-analysis total.

Coral Bay begin the chase against Jade Sinclair. Aila Rowan survives three balls, then Jade bowls her at 0.4. The first partnership contains one extra and no batter runs. Television keeps the stump camera up while Nia Brooke enters, making the incoming batter a more reliable boundary than the repeated image. Jade walks past mid-off to reset her mark, while the captain moves a catcher from point to the cordon. The radio analyst talks about the damp length and does not revisit the wicket ownership.

The production truck cuts briefly to the toss interview and returns with Nia waiting over a review. No additional ball has occurred during the insert, and the score strip is deliberately hidden. Back on the live decision, Jade traps Nia lbw on the next legal ball. That partnership contains no run of any kind. The gallery then returns to Aila's broken stumps while explaining Nia's decision, so two distinct live wickets are followed by an old picture rather than by a third dismissal. Maris takes several deliveries to settle, and the commentators turn to her defensive setup and Emilia's calling. The generic replay caption disappears before the next wicket.

Lara Holt joins Emilia. Each batter contributes one and their interval has no extras. Nora Finch catches Lara from Tara Quinn at 6.2. The live blog briefly attaches Jade's generic caption to the paragraph, but the delivery and catch sequence clearly belong to Tara.

Sienna Park becomes Emilia's longest-lasting partner. Sienna's batting share reaches four. A partnership operator opens an extras box at five, then marks it for review because its first entry may have crossed the previous wicket boundary. Emilia's contribution is kept on another feed.

Emilia's draft component in the Sienna stand reaches ten. The scorer notices that a wide shown before the stand's settled boundary has also been credited to Emilia by the television operator. She flags the batter component but delays the decision until the over transitions can be compared.

A timeout interrupts that check. Television shows Sienna defending, then Aila's opening dismissal, then Sienna again. Jade is now fielding at cover, so the inserted Aila clip cannot add to Jade's live spell. The radio team discusses the surface rather than presenting any wicket list.

Ivy Stone bowls Sienna at 12.1. That ball fixes the fifth partnership's endpoint. The board updates the wicket count before the partnership ribbon, and the latter remains one run above the scorer's component ledger. No replacement stand value is shown.

The batter-side correction arrives two overs later. The carried wide is removed from Emilia's draft share in the Sienna partnership, putting that component one below ten. Sienna's contribution remains unchanged. The extras-side review is still open, so the partnership cannot yet be solved locally.

Faye Turner faces two balls and scores nothing; Emilia also adds nothing in that stand, which has no extras. Ivy bowls Faye. A Sienna replay occupies the screen during the next batter's walk, but the incoming Faye-to-Bella transition proves that live play has advanced.

Bella Marsh also contributes nothing, as does Emilia during their brief partnership. One extra occurs before Ivy bowls Bella at the end of the over. The repeated Sienna celebration is shown once more between deliveries and must remain attached to the earlier wicket.

Only after Bella leaves does the interval clerk settle the Sienna-Emilia extras component. The fifth partnership had inherited one wide from the preceding display, so its provisional five is reduced by one. That correction is separated from both batter contributions and from Sienna's dismissal marker.

Celeste Reed and Emilia add a small stand. Celeste supplies one, Emilia one, and one extra occurs before Rowan catches Celeste from Tara at 14.2. The extra is assigned solely to this eighth partnership interval, away from the already corrected fifth interval.

Ruth Elms stays longer. Ruth contributes three, Emilia six, and the interval contains one extra. Mira Vale bowls Ruth. The team-score line at that dismissal reads thirty-eight, while the over sheet holding its ball marker is temporarily with another clerk. Priya Cove enters as the final partner. The terminal delivery has not yet occurred.

A scorer now checks the chase partnership partitions. The sixth interval had no extras, the seventh had one, the eighth had one and the ninth had one. She does not revisit the first five or say what the final interval will contain, leaving the aggregate distributed across the innings. A separate fall clerk confirms that Ruth followed eight earlier dismissals and is therefore the ninth wicket, without restating the score.

Priya begins with a boundary. Her contribution across the final partnership eventually reaches five, although the tight camera shows the boundary twice. Emilia's contribution is not stated at this point. The television ticker provisionally treats the second angle as fresh play and carries the chase four runs beyond its event ledger.

The scorer compares fielder positions and retracts the duplicate boundary increment. The scoreboard returns to the roll-forward built from the ninth-wicket state. This correction occurs before the last wicket and supplies no new legal ball. Much later, the over-sheet clerk returns and identifies Ruth's dismissal marker as 16.5, without repeating either its score or wicket ordinal.

The final partnership contains no extras. That zero is entered only after the replay correction, well away from the earlier partnership-extra sequence. Priya remains on strike for part of the passage, and Emilia's personal ledger is still open.

Emilia adds one in the final stand. Her earlier contributions are spread over Maris, Lara, Sienna, Faye, Bella, Celeste and Ruth, including the revised Sienna component and two explicit zero intervals. No personal total is displayed.

At 17.4 Emilia drives Mira and Jade takes the catch. A provisional production analysis assigns the dismissal to Jade because its parser follows the catcher name. The ground scorer revises the bowling ownership to Mira while preserving the dismissal itself. The ball is logged at 17.4 on the over sheet, with no wicket ordinal printed beside it.

Priya remains not out and no further delivery is bowled. Only after play has stopped does the fall clerk close Emilia's line as the tenth wicket, without restating the score or delivery. A live-blog footer still contains the four replay runs for several seconds, then disappears. The official state therefore depends on the earlier ninth-wicket score, the two separated batter contributions, the zero-extra final interval, the replay retraction, the tenth-wicket order and the delivery marker.

The radio closes by confirming Meadowridge's victory and Jade as player of the match, without repeating the winning margin. The broadcast signs off before the detailed cards are posted, with the scorer still carrying the reconciled worksheets toward the pavilion.

documents.text:
There is a warm crosswind at South Meridian Institute Ground, and Shoreline Rangers begin with the television director already warning that the scoring ribbon is taking numbers from a live scorer and a delayed graphics cache. Finn Archer drives the first loose ball and keeps most of the strike while Leo Marsh settles. A glance off the pad is initially entered to Finn. The umpire is partly hidden behind Leo, so the booth carries Finn's opening-stand contribution as forty. No correction appears before the next over. The old figure also goes into the wagon-wheel thumbnail, where it will survive longer than the live commentary. Nothing about this early panel can yet be treated as a closed personal total.

Leo's own innings ends at 8.4 when he is caught by Aiden Scott from Zane Cooper. The board behind the bowler has Shoreline on sixty-two for one. Two byes have already been signalled during the opening passage, but they are mentioned only in an exchange about the keeper's footwork. Rory Blake comes in, blocks his first ball, and loses off stump to Zane on the next. The score has not moved between the wickets. The new batter waits at the rope while the director shows Rory's dismissal from behind the arm, then from square leg. A feed process logs the second view as another item even though it contains the same batter, delivery and wicket state.

Miles Carter walks out after Rory. The innings is now sixty-two for two, a state shown only on the sightscreen. Finn and Miles settle through singles and a late cut. Finn's contribution inside this association reaches thirty-six on the provisional stand card, but Miles's share and the extras box are absent from that picture. The second angle of Rory's wicket returns while the pair are batting. It remains an archival view: there was no run during Rory's stay, and the new partnership is already under way.

Dylan Vale is padded up when the camera catches a scoring argument near the boundary. Five extras have accumulated during the Finn-Miles association. A timing marker appears to have crossed the coming wicket boundary, yet the operator queues the repair without saying which personal panel will change. The main ribbon disappears before either batter's settled contribution is shown. Miles is later caught by Julian Vale from Aiden Scott, while a cropped caption saying only “Miles caught” creates a surname trap for the interval bowling montage.

Dylan Vale begins with four runs in the brief passage before Finn's dismissal. Miles Benton finds Finn's edge, and Arin Wells completes the catch. This is a valid Benton dismissal, although no running wicket total is attached to his name. The camera replays the edge twice from different angles. Those pictures describe one departure. The broadcaster does not disclose whether Finn added anything after Miles Carter left; that small component remains unresolved until the closing archive review.

Only after Finn has left does the scorer settle the opening pad incident. The side-on picture shows no bat, and the missed signal is confirmed as a leg bye. The team total is untouched. Finn's opening contribution therefore becomes one lower than the forty first shown. The graphics cache keeps the old number in an archival panel, but the live contribution ledger changes. This correction is separated from the Finn-Miles boundary repair: one concerns attribution in the opening stand, the other concerns a run placed after Miles's wicket. Treating them as the same repair would lose the evidence needed to close Finn's innings.

Dylan begins a longer rebuild with Connor Wells. A quick single is placed against Dylan, taking his provisional contribution in this stand to fourteen. Several overs later, during a crowd shot, the scorer receives a low replay showing that the ball brushed the pad without touching the bat. The missed leg-bye signal moves one unit out of Dylan's column. Connor is eventually bowled by Zane Cooper with a ball that also moves into off stump. It resembles Rory's dismissal in wording and camera angle, yet the other batter is Dylan, the innings is much further advanced, and the partnership state is different.
